intro.text: The City of Bells, an open, multicultural city on Roshar named for the bells that hang throughout it.
An independent Vorin city-state on Roshar, the City of Bells, home to the Palanaeum and famous for its hospitals.
An independent city-state, the City of Bells, which under Queen Savrahalidem declared itself neutral in the war.
The City of Bells, destroyed by a tidal wave sent by Odium.

description.text: Kharbranth turns no one away for their nation or standing, so people from all over Roshar make their homes there.

Bells hang everywhere, supposedly to warn of highstorms that are said to be too gentle to notice here, and their ringing reaches even deep in the Conclave. The blocky buildings, built on or carved from the mountain, are painted in bright colours that show their purpose.
Kharbranth is thought safe, though violent crime has sometimes gone unpoliced, and some suspect corruption in the city watch.

Its many hospitals, funded by the Palanaeum's entrance fees, treat anyone regardless of eye color, rank or nationality, and King Taravangian is a warmly welcomed visitor. The Great Concourse offers the best medical training on Roshar, with costly tuition and hard entrance exams.

Kharbranth is ruled by a monarch together with a council, and the crown can pass down through either the male or the female line. The monarch can put forward and steer policy, deals with other nations and has some direct power over how laws are carried out.

items.text: Kharbranth turns no one away for their nation or standing, so people from all over Roshar make their homes there.
Unlike Alethkar, Kharbranth allows no human slaves, though it still puts parshmen to work without pay.

Kharbranth counts among the five Vorin nations. Its ardentia carries weight in the city, stays in touch with Vorin leaders in the east, and runs and staffs the Palanaeum. Not every devotary is present (there are no ardents of Sincerity), and the ardents own no Soulcasters. Those who don't follow Vorinism mostly keep their views to themselves.
Kharbranth has restaurants, and soup is the favourite midday meal.

Kharbranth keeps its standing army small, to seem harmless. It seldom goes to war and sends medical aid to both sides of a conflict, with its soldiers guarding these missions. It has no true navy, but can take over merchant ships in an emergency, and its soldiers wear burnt orange and white.

Like most of Roshar, Kharbranth trades in spheres: glass beads set with gems that give light when infused, worth more or less by the kind and size of the stone, from the diamond chip up to the emerald broam. The Palanaeum doubles as the royal treasury, and the city's emeralds light its halls.

Kharbranth began as a pirate town and grew into a city over decades; some say it is older than the Last Desolation. In the time of the Silver Kingdoms its land would have belonged to Thalath, and it has been Vorin since at least the Hierocracy.
The two great caverns of the Palanaeum are older than the city, with the rooms for its books cut later; some believe the Dawnsingers made them. A fire once destroyed part of the collection.
As a young courier, Lirin travelled to Kharbranth, and later he learned medicine from Vathe, who had trained at the Great Concourse.
Lirin hoped to send Kaladin to Kharbranth to train as a surgeon at sixteen, and he and Hesina kept a hoard of spheres to pay for it.

In 1173, Jasnah Kholin came to Kharbranth to study in the Palanaeum. Shallan Davar, who had chased her for six months, caught up with her in the Conclave and was eventually accepted as her ward, secretly meaning to swap her family's broken Soulcaster for Jasnah's.
Jasnah freed Taravangian's granddaughter, trapped by a cave-in in the palace, and in return was allowed into the Palanaeum.

Late one night, Jasnah led Shallan down a street near the theatre district where thieves had been robbing and killing people, and when four men attacked, she Soulcast them. Back at the Conclave, Shallan swapped Jasnah's Soulcaster for her broken one.
Jasnah eventually forgave Shallan and took her back, and the two left Kharbranth for the Shattered Plains aboard the Wind's Pleasure.

When Szeth came to Kharbranth to kill its king, the last name on his list, Taravangian revealed that he held Szeth's oathstone and had ordered all the killings, showed him a hidden hospital where the dying were gathered, and sent him to kill Dalinar Kholin.
Just before the Everstorm, Taravangian ordered the city's enslaved parshmen sent away; some were shipped to the Frostlands and woke in an unfamiliar land with nothing.
After the battle at Thaylen City, Taravangian admitted to Dalinar that Kharbranth had been behind Szeth's killings across Roshar.
Kaladin stopped for a night in Kharbranth on his way to Alethkar and took infused gemstones from the royal treasury for the journey.

The new queen, Savrahalidem, condemned her father's actions and withdrew Kharbranth from every alliance, declaring it neutral and returning to its role of giving medical aid to anyone. Dalinar blockaded its waters but would not risk a costly land attack.
Cultivation threatened Taravangian's family to press him toward peace. He answered by sending a tidal wave that destroyed Kharbranth.
Retribution kept a replica of Kharbranth in the Spiritual Realm. He had secretly moved the citizens there before the destruction and removed their memories of it.

told.title: The Palanaeum's caverns
told.text: The two great caverns of the Palanaeum are older than the city; the rooms that hold its books were cut once people had settled there. How the caverns were made is unknown, though some credit the Dawnsingers. A fire has since burned part of the collection.

told.title: An ancient city
told.text: Rumour has it that Kharbranth predates the Last Desolation, and one account even dates its founding to the shadowdays.

told.title: Under the Hierocracy
told.text: Kharbranth belonged to the Hierocracy, a wide Vorin realm that also took in Jah Keved and the lands that became Alethkar and Thaylenah. After the Hierocracy fell in the War of Loss, Kharbranth kept close alliances with the other Vorin nations.

told.title: Lirin's journey
told.text: As a young courier, Lirin travelled to Kharbranth and saw something of the world's peoples. He learned medicine from Vathe, a surgeon trained at the city's Great Concourse.

told.title: A place for Kaladin
told.text: Lirin hoped his son Kaladin could train as a surgeon in Kharbranth once he turned sixteen, and kept a hoard of spheres to pay for it. When Roshone arrived in Hearthstone, Lirin wrote to the city's surgeons asking that Kaladin be allowed to take the entrance tests early; they said no.

told.title: The Diagram
told.text: Gavilar Kholin had told Taravangian that his visions demanded a united world. Taravangian asked the Nightwatcher for the capacity to save humankind, and on one day of towering intelligence he wrote the predictions that became the Diagram, followed in secret by a group of the same name. Because his wits change from day to day, he is tested each morning to settle what he may do.

On the night he died, Gavilar Kholin told Taravangian of visions warning that the world must unite to survive the coming Desolation. Taravangian went to the Nightwatcher and begged for the power to save Roshar. On one day of towering intelligence he wrote the predictions that became the Diagram, followed in secret by a group of the same name. The gift had a curse: he could be brilliant or compassionate, but never both at once.

told.title: The secret hospital
told.text: The king kept a secret hospital where dying patients were slowly bled so that the words they spoke as they died could be written down. He believed those words might hold the key to saving everyone.

Deep in the Conclave, the Silent Gatherers ran hidden hospitals where the terminally ill and the very poor were brought to be killed, so that their Death Rattles could add to the Diagram's predictions.

Deep in the Conclave, the Silent Gatherers ran hidden hospitals where the terminally ill and the very poor were brought to be killed, so that their Death Rattles could add to the Diagram's predictions. The Death Rattles grew rarer from late 1173 and stopped altogether in 1174, but the hospitals kept working.

told.title: A key to the Palanaeum
told.text: Jasnah Kholin freed Taravangian's granddaughter, trapped by a cave-in deep inside the palace, and in return the king let her into the Palanaeum.

told.title: Shallan becomes a ward
told.text: Jasnah had come in 1173 to research in the Palanaeum. Shallan Davar, who had been chasing her for six months, found her in the Conclave and won a place as her ward, though her real aim was to swap her family's broken Soulcaster for Jasnah's.

told.title: The alley
told.text: One night Jasnah took Shallan down a street near the theatre district where robbers had been killing people, and when four men attacked she Soulcast them all. Back at the Conclave, Shallan swapped her broken Soulcaster for Jasnah's.

told.title: Poisoned bread
told.text: When a goblet turned to blood in her hands, Shallan cut her own arm to hide it and was taken to a hospital. There the ardent Kabsal offered bread poisoned to kill Jasnah. Shallan ate it, and Jasnah saved her by Soulcasting her blood, finding out about the stolen Soulcaster.

told.title: Leaving Kharbranth
told.text: Jasnah forgave Shallan and took her back as her ward, and the two sailed from Kharbranth for the Shattered Plains on the Wind's Pleasure.

told.title: The assassin's master
told.text: Szeth's killings of rulers and officials across Roshar, the king of Jah Keved among them, were ordered by Taravangian, who held the assassin's oathstone and put his own name on the list to avoid suspicion. When Szeth came to kill him, the king revealed himself as his master and sent him after Dalinar Kholin.

told.title: King of Jah Keved
told.text: Taravangian had a hand in starting Jah Keved's civil war, then sent food, medicine and healers to tend the wounded of every side. As the war ended, the dying King Valam named him heir, making him king of Jah Keved as well.

told.title: Answering Dalinar
told.text: When Dalinar Kholin asked the rulers of Roshar for help against the Voidbringers, Taravangian alone agreed at once, bringing Kharbranth and Jah Keved into alliance with Alethkar.

When Dalinar Kholin asked the rulers of Roshar for help against the Voidbringers, Taravangian alone agreed at once, bringing Kharbranth and Jah Keved into alliance with Alethkar. He went to Urithiru and left a scribe to run the city, and abroad many took him for a figurehead, with the true power held by that scribe or by his head scribe, Adrotagia.

told.title: Playing both sides
told.text: The alliance gave Taravangian and the Diagram a way into Urithiru and into how the coalition was run. They spied on its members and spread false stories to split it, and before Thaylen Field they secretly leaked Dalinar's meeting with Odium, the highking proposal and the Eila Stele translation. During that battle Malata quietly unlocked the Kholinar Oathgate, hindering the coalition's troop movements.

told.title: Taravangian's confession
told.text: After the battle, Taravangian confessed to Dalinar that Szeth's killings across Roshar had been Kharbranth's doing. He had gone looking for the assassin after an ardent called Dova, who he believed was the Herald Battah'Elin, warned him that a Desolation was near.

told.title: A bargain with Odium
told.text: During the Everstorm, Taravangian struck a deal with Odium: the Diagram's loyalty in return for sparing Kharbranth and its people in the war ahead.

told.title: Kaladin passes through
told.text: On his way to Alethkar, Kaladin stopped for a night in Kharbranth and drew infused gemstones from the royal treasury for the journey.

told.title: The Diagram disbanded
told.text: Kharbranth stayed in the coalition but often argued against its battle plans, while Taravangian's inner circle drifted home to Kharbranth at his request. Ready to turn on the coalition, he disbanded the Diagram and had its work in the city taken apart, so that the city would not be punished for his betrayal.

Kharbranth stayed in the coalition but often argued against its battle plans, while Taravangian's inner circle drifted home to Kharbranth at his request. Ready to turn on the coalition, he disbanded the Diagram, had its work in the city taken apart and removed everyone tied to it from government, so that the city would not be punished for his betrayal.

told.title: The betrayal at Emul
told.text: In Emul, Taravangian sent the order for his armies to turn on the coalition, and within minutes he was arrested.

In Emul, Taravangian sent the order for his armies to turn on the coalition, and within minutes he was arrested. From prison he told Dalinar that, sure the coalition would lose, he had seen no other way to save Kharbranth.

told.title: Queen Savrahalidem
told.text: Taravangian's daughter Savrahalidem, whom he had kept out of the Diagram so she would share none of the blame, became queen. She condemned her father, pulled Kharbranth out of every alliance and declared it neutral, going back to healing anyone in need. Dalinar blockaded the city's waters but would not risk a costly attack on land.

told.title: Swept away
told.text: Cultivation sent agents into Kharbranth and threatened to kill Taravangian's family unless he made peace with the coalition. To prove he could not be cowed, he called up a huge tidal wave that wiped out the city.

told.title: A city kept safe
told.text: While Cultivation looked away, Retribution had quietly moved Kharbranth's people into a copy of the city he made in the Spiritual Realm, taking away their memories of its destruction.
